text:
# Direct volume ray casting

Also called: Ray casting, Backward ray marching, Image-order volume rendering

## Overview
Direct volume ray casting is an [image-order rendering](#16-image-order-rendering.md) technique that visualizes 3D scalar data by treating the volume as a translucent medium, integrating emission and absorption along rays cast from the camera through each pixel [S3, S4, S5, unofficial]. Unlike surface-based methods that extract explicit geometry, it renders the entire volume implicitly, allowing internal structures to be seen through outer layers [S3, unofficial]. It differs from object-order methods (like [splatting](#23-splatting.md)) by computing the final pixel color via a per-ray integration loop, which naturally supports early ray termination and view-dependent shading [S4, S9, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The method implements the emission-absorption [optical model](#33-optical-models.md), computing the light intensity reaching the eye by integrating radiative energy along a ray through the scalar volume [S1, S5, S9, unofficial]. The process follows a strict pipeline for each pixel: ray generation, sampling, classification (transfer function application), shading, and [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) [S4, S34, unofficial].

### Ray Generation and Discretization
For each pixel, a ray $r(t) = \mathbf{o} + t\mathbf{d}$ is defined, where $\mathbf{o}$ is the camera origin and $\mathbf{d}$ is the direction [S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8, S9, S10, S11, S12, S13, S14, S15, S16, S17, S18, S19, S20, S21, S22, S23, S24, S25, S26, S27, S28, S29, S30, S31, S32, S33, S34, S35, S36, S37, S38, S39, S40, S41, S42, S43, S44, S45, S46, S47, S48, S49, S50, S51, S52, S53, S54, S55, S56, S57, S58, S59, S60, S61, S62, S63, S64, S65, S66, S67, S68, S69, S70, S71, S72, S73, S74, S75, S76, S77, S78, S79, S80, S81, S82, S83, S84, S85, S86, S87, S88, S89, S90, S91, S92, S93, S94, S95, S96, S97, S98, S99, S100]. The ray is intersected with the volume domain (typically an axis-aligned bounding box) to determine the entry parameter $t_{start}$ and exit parameter $t_{end}$ [S1, S7, S15, S22, S33, S55, unofficial]. The segment $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$ is discretized into $N$ samples at equidistant intervals $\Delta t$ [S4, S8, S9, S16, S33, S40, unofficial]. The step size $\Delta t$ is often chosen to ensure at least one sample per voxel along the fastest axis to minimize aliasing, though adaptive stepping is also used [S36, unofficial][S46, abstract only, unofficial].

### Sampling and Interpolation
At each sample point $\mathbf{p}_i = r(t_i)$, the scalar volume value $V(\mathbf{p}_i)$ is reconstructed from the discrete voxel grid [S6, S7, S33, unofficial][S44, book]. Trilinear interpolation is the standard [reconstruction filter](#817-interpolation-schemes-for-volume-rendering.md) for high-quality rendering, combining the eight surrounding voxels [S6, S7, S33, S40, unofficial]. [Nearest-neighbor interpolation](#5891-nearest-neighbor-interpolation.md) is used for performance or specific artifact styles [S43, unofficial][S44, book]. The interpolated value represents the local density or material property [S9, S18, unofficial].

### Classification (Transfer Function)
The scalar value $d_i = V(\mathbf{p}_i)$ is mapped to optical properties: color $C_i$ and opacity $\alpha_i$ [S2, S5, S11, S12, S25, S29, S31, S34, unofficial]. This mapping is defined by a transfer function $T(d_i)$ [S2, S5, S2789]. [Pre-classification](#6103-pre-classification.md) maps scalar values to RGBA before interpolation, while post-classification interpolates scalars first and then applies the transfer function [S4, unofficial][S44, book]. The opacity $\alpha_i$ determines the fraction of light absorbed or scattered at the sample [S18, S23, S51, unofficial].

### Compositing (Front-to-Back Integration)
The final pixel color $C_{final}$ is computed by integrating contributions from all samples along the ray from front to back ($t_{start}$ to $t_{end}$) [S1, S12, S16, S23, S24, S43, S50, S51, unofficial]. The standard compositing equation ([over operator](#3360-front-to-back-compositing-over-operator.md)) updates the accumulated color $C'$ and accumulated opacity $\alpha'$ for each sample $i$:

$$
C'_{i} = C'_{i-1} + (1 - \alpha'_{i-1}) \alpha_i C_i
$$
$$
\alpha'_{i} = \alpha'_{i-1} + (1 - \alpha'_{i-1}) \alpha_i
$$

where $C'_0 = 0$ and $\alpha'_0 = 0$ [S12, S43, S50, unofficial]. The term $(1 - \alpha'_{i-1})$ represents the transmittance (light reaching the current sample) [S1, S51, unofficial]. If $\alpha'$ reaches 1 (or a threshold close to it), the ray can be terminated early, as subsequent samples are fully occluded [S9, S12, S27, unofficial].

### Shading
[Shading models](#837-shading-models.md) are applied to enhance depth perception. Common techniques include Phong or Blinn-Phong shading, which use the gradient of the volume data $\nabla V$ to compute surface normals for [lighting calculations](#2056-lighting-models.md) [S14, S15, S30, unofficial][S54]. The gradient is typically estimated using central differences or [Sobel operators](#1416-sobel-operator.md) on the interpolated scalar field [S14, S30, unofficial][S54].

## Subtopics

### [Direct Volume Rendering](1184-direct-volume-rendering.md)
The core implementation of the [emission-absorption model](#927-emission-absorption-model.md), treating the volume as a translucent gel. It distinguishes itself by visualizing the entire volume without extracting surfaces.

### [Opacity Correction for Slice Count Invariance](1277-opacity-correction-for-slice-count-invariance.md)
Corrects the opacity $\alpha_i$ to ensure visual consistency regardless of the sampling rate, solving the brightness artifact where denser sampling appears brighter.

### [Back-face rasterized volume rendering](1296-back-face-rasterized-volume-rendering.md)
Uses GPU rasterization of the volume's bounding box front and back faces to determine ray entry/exit points, replacing analytical intersection calculations.

### [Neural volume rendering](1576-neural-volume-rendering.md)
Replaces the explicit voxel grid with a continuous 5D neural function (MLP) that predicts density and color, enabling differentiable rendering and novel view synthesis.

### [Hybrid Gradient Volume Raycasting with Lasso Masking](2059-hybrid-gradient-volume-raycasting-with-lasso-masking.md)
Combines pre-computed Hounsfield Unit gradients for lighting with a hybrid shading model, applying Phong lighting only where opacity changes are significant.

### [Temporal Accumulation (Closest Hit)](2080-temporal-accumulation-closest-hit.md)
Stabilizes noisy rendering by blending current frames with history, specifically selecting the closest hit to prevent ghosting from disoccluded structures.

### [Alpha-to-Weight Computation (Forward)](2373-alpha-to-weight-computation-forward.md)
Computes per-sample weights and transmittance for front-to-back compositing from raw alpha values, segmenting samples by ray ID for efficient GPU processing.

### [Volumetric Smoke Rendering with Worley Noise and Light Maps](2447-volumetric-smoke-rendering-with-worley-noise-and-light-maps.md)
Uses [Worley noise](#1726-worley-noise.md) for density and light maps for scattering in real-time smoke rendering, differing from standard DVR by using procedural noise instead of scalar data.

### [Compositing and Blending](2515-compositing-and-blending.md)
The family of techniques for integrating optical properties (color/opacity) along a ray, solving the problem of combining semi-transparent samples into a single pixel value.

### [Tiled Ray Marching with Grid Sampling](2586-tiled-ray-marching-with-grid-sampling.md)
Renders volumes by tiling the image to manage memory, using grid sampling for density and accumulating attenuation.

### [Surface Rendering Pipeline](2614-surface-rendering-pipeline.md)
A mode that stops at the first voxel above a threshold and shades it, generating no mesh but avoiding the "fuzzy" look of full volume rendering.

### [Energy Region Compositing](2717-energy-region-compositing.md)
Composites multiple energy volumes within a region defined by a magnitude volume, applying thresholds before compositing.

### [Window/Level Volume Raycasting with Bricking](2775-window-level-volume-raycasting-with-bricking.md)
Accelerates traversal by decomposing data into bricks and applying window/level transfer functions, supporting LQ/HQ modes.

### [Interpolation and Sampling Techniques](2787-interpolation-and-sampling-techniques.md)
Provides mechanisms to reconstruct continuous fields from discrete voxels, solving discretization artifacts like aliasing.

### [Ray Marching and Discretization](2788-ray-marching-and-discretization.md)
The fundamental iterative algorithm for approximating the volume rendering integral by accumulating optical properties at discrete points.

### [Transfer Function and Opacity Mapping](2789-transfer-function-and-opacity-mapping.md)
Defines the mapping from scalar data to RGBA attributes, solving the semantic interpretation of raw numerical data.

### [Doppler Volume Rendering](3536-doppler-volume-rendering.md)
Accounts for the Doppler effect of light in moving media, emitting/attenuating light at shifted wavelengths based on a 3D velocity field.

### [Multiresolution Volume Rendering](3541-multiresolution-volume-rendering.md)
Uses a hierarchy of resolutions (e.g., wavelets) for adaptive integration and [early termination](#4675-early-termination.md), reducing cost for large datasets.

### [Next Event Estimation for Emissive Volumes](3557-next-event-estimation-for-emissive-volumes.md)
Samples light sources directly within participating media to reduce noise in path tracing, differing from fixed-step casting.

### [Classified Volume Rendering](3590-classified-volume-rendering.md)
Precomputes a run-length encoded structure of classified voxels to enable rapid rendering with fixed classification but arbitrary shading.

### [Parallel Domain-Decomposed Ray Casting](3625-parallel-domain-decomposed-ray-casting.md)
Distributes the volume across MPI processes for distributed-memory parallelization, with each process rendering its sub-volume chunk.

### [Front-to-Back Volume Ray Casting with HSV Shading and SOS/Attenuation/Reflection Filtering](4324-front-to-back-volume-ray-casting-with-hsv-shading-and-sos-at.md)
Uses fixed steps and specific filtering (SOS, attenuation, reflection) combined with HSV shading.

### [LOS-integration for visualization](4807-los-integration-for-visualization.md)
Integrates scalar physical quantities (emissivity/density) along rays, often from neural networks, outputting integrals rather than color.

### [Hierarchical Sampling](4865-hierarchical-sampling.md)
Uses a coarse estimate to guide fine sample placement via importance sampling, solving inefficient [uniform sampling](#1261-uniform-ray-sampling.md).

### [Volumetric Rendering with Spherical Harmonics](4962-volumetric-rendering-with-spherical-harmonics.md)
Represents the volume as sparse grid SH coefficients to compute color and transmittance, supporting background compositing.

### [Monte Carlo Path Tracing for Volume Rendering](4980-monte-carlo-path-tracing-for-volume-rendering.md)
Simulates light transport stochastically, tracing random paths and scattering events, unlike fixed-step casting.

### [Customization Volume Integration](5291-customization-volume-integration.md)
Integrates a pre-computed "customization volume" to apply position-dependent modifications like [gamma correction](#2225-gamma-correction.md).

### [Pre-integrated Volume Rendering](5327-pre-integrated-volume-rendering.md)
Pre-computes the rendering integral for ray segments into a lookup table (LUT) to accelerate runtime, solving high computational cost.

### [Hardware-Accelerated Volume Rendering](5616-hardware-accelerated-volume-rendering.md)
Offloads ray casting and compositing to specialized hardware (GPUs), using 3D textures and hardware interpolation units.

### [Two-pass and Multi-pass Techniques](6224-two-pass-and-multi-pass-techniques.md)
Decouples light attenuation (depth pass) from color compositing (eye pass) to efficiently compute accurate volumetric lighting.

### [Slice-based and Proxy Geometry Rendering](6225-slice-based-and-proxy-geometry-rendering.md)
Rasterizes 2D proxy geometry (slices) inside the volume to perform sampling and compositing, solving hardware limitations.

### [Projection and MIP Techniques](6305-projection-and-mip-techniques.md)
Projects a single scalar value (e.g., maximum) along each ray, rather than integrating emission/absorption [Direct volume ray casting](19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md).

### [GPU Ray Casting for Light Field Display](6503-gpu-ray-casting-for-light-field-display.md)
Generates per-pixel ray parameters for multi-viewer 3D visualization using MCOP projection, addressing light field display challenges.

### [WebGL Multi-pass Ray-casting with 3D Geometry Intersection](6575-webgl-multi-pass-ray-casting-with-3d-geometry-intersection.md)
Integrates 3D meshes with volumes in WebGL using a five-pass pipeline to handle lack of native 3D texture support.

### [TVAM Integrator](6814-tvam-integrator.md)
Handles projector ray sampling and time sampling for volumetric additive manufacturing integrators.

### Forward Mapping
A variant that projects each voxel directly onto the image plane, relying on traversal order for hidden surface removal [S56, unofficial]. It determines the foremost corner voxel and establishes a traversal order (rows, columns, slices) such that the foremost voxel is visited last [S56, unofficial].

### Gradient Shading for Turbulent Flow Visualization
Applies solid-texture-mapping to map one velocity component onto another, then applies [gradient shading](#6896-gradient-based-shading.md) with ambient, diffuse, specular, and glossiness lighting to solve the "fuzzy" look of turbulent flow data [S57].

### Raw Volume Rendering
A slower algorithm that does not use precomputed data structures like [min-max octrees](#6428-flat-blocking-multi-resolution-volume-rendering.md), useful only for single renderings [S58].

### Spherical Volume Rendering with Adaptive Ray Casting
Uses a spherical mosaic as proxy geometry and adaptive sampling based on depth distribution and data change rate to improve efficiency for ocean scalar fields [S46, abstract only, unofficial].

### Svox1 Rendering Formula (Nearest-Neighbor)
Implements the Svox1 rendering formula using nearest-neighbor interpolation with infinitely many steps, including forward, backward, and fused variants [S59, unofficial].

### MCOP GPU Ray-Casting Pipeline
Uses Mixed Camera and Object Perspective (MCOP) projection to render light fields, bypassing rasterizer interpolation limitations by computing ray entry/direction in the fragment shader [S60].

### GPU-accelerated ray casting with volumetric lenses
Calculates ray directions using lens rules (feature-based, sampling-rate-based, angular) and implements a four-pass fragment program structure for magnifier/angular lenses [S61].

## Background
Direct volume ray casting was pioneered by Marc Levoy in his seminal 1988 paper "Display of Surfaces from Volume Data" [S8, S9, unofficial]. Levoy coined the term and defined the standard visualization pipeline ([classification, shading](#2278-classification-and-shading.md), compositing) [S8, unofficial]. The method was initially developed for CPU-based rendering and later adapted for GPU [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) in the early 2000s (e.g., Roettger et al. 2003, Stegmaier et al. 2004) as fragment shader capabilities improved [S5, unofficial]. It remains the foundational technique for interactive volume visualization in medical imaging and scientific visualization [S4, S9, S26, unofficial].
